model.note: Weights were fitted by least squares against Ash's own ratings of 31 books she has already read. Predicted values are on her own 0-5 Overall scale. Re-fit whenever she rates something new.

anchors.title: The Serpent and the Wings of Night
anchors.author: Carissa Broadbent

anchors.title: A Court of Thorns and Roses
anchors.author: Sarah J. Maas
anchors.series: A Court of Thorns and Roses

catalog.title: A Dowry of Blood
catalog.author: S.T. Gibson
catalog.povNote: second person epistolary, written by Constanta as a long letter addressed to the husband she killed
catalog.hook: Dracula's first bride writes to her dead husband across five centuries, recounting how he made her, isolated her, and how she and his other two consorts finally ended him.
catalog.caution: It is the closest thing here to dark romance and it is short, but the second-person letter format keeps the reader at arm's length and it summarizes centuries rather than dramatizing scenes, so it can feel like a beautiful synopsis instead of a story.

catalog.title: Daughter of Smoke & Bone
catalog.author: Laini Taylor
catalog.povNote: third person centered on Karou, opening out to Akiva and a long past-life section in the back half
tropes: secret errands for a monster father figure
catalog.hook: A blue-haired art student in Prague who runs errands collecting teeth for her chimaera family meets the seraph sent to destroy them, and learns what she actually is.
catalog.caution: The prose is the best argument for this lane and the reveal is a genuine gut punch, but the middle third abandons the present-day plot entirely for a long flashback, and Karou's fate is more discovered than chosen, which edges toward the passivity she hated in ACOTAR.

catalog.title: The Ballad of Falling Dragons
catalog.author: Sarah A. Parker
catalog.setting: a dying world of caged dragons, moon-magic and buried memory
catalog.povNote: Raeve and Kaan anchor it but the cast widens to five or six narrators, including the antagonist
catalog.hook: The second Moonfall book, in which the assassin Raeve confronts what was taken out of her head and the dragons start falling out of the sky.
catalog.caution: Requires When the Moon Hatched (2024) first, and that book's invented dialect and withheld information are a slow, deliberately disorienting on-ramp; the opposite of Fourth Wing's opening chapters.

catalog.title: Sick Fux
catalog.author: Tillie Cole
catalog.povNote: dual first-person from two survivors sharing one delusion, so the unreliability is built into both voices
catalog.hook: Two childhood abuse survivors reunite after eleven years apart and go on a revenge spree against the people who destroyed them, narrating it through a shared Wonderland delusion.
catalog.caution: The CSA is depicted on the page in graphic detail, not referenced; this is the one on the list most likely to be a hard stop regardless of how dark she reads.

catalog.title: Harvest Season
catalog.author: Brynne Weaver
catalog.setting: Cape Carnage in the aftermath, with true-crime tourists flooding the town
catalog.povNote: Harper and Nolan alternate as before, with chapters from the antagonist La Plume opening up the threat from the other side
tropes: cat and mouse with law enforcement
catalog.hook: The sequel to Tourist Season, in which the couple's body count catches up with them and a third narrator starts hunting them both.
catalog.caution: Ends on a hard cliffhanger with book three unpublished, and she has already been burned by waiting on a series (From Blood and Ash); this is a two-book commitment with no landing in sight.

catalog.title: House of Hollow
catalog.author: Krystal Sutherland
catalog.povNote: first person from Iris, the youngest of three sisters, with interleaved flashbacks to the month they all went missing
catalog.hook: Three sisters who vanished as children and returned unnervingly changed are forced to confront what happened to them when the eldest disappears again, leaving a trail of rot and black flowers through London.
catalog.caution: Under 300 pages and it moves, which suits her, but the romance is negligible and the ending is more unsettling than cathartic, so the gut punch may read as bleak rather than earned.

catalog.title: Take Me with You
catalog.author: Nina G. Jones
catalog.povNote: dual first-person from the home invader and the woman he takes, his chapters unflinchingly inside his logic
catalog.hook: A methodical night stalker breaks into a woman's house and she offers herself in place of her disabled brother, beginning a long captivity that neither of them survives unchanged.
catalog.caution: The writing is the best-regarded thing about it, but the FMC spends most of the book without options; after her ACOTAR complaint, a heroine who cannot act is the fastest way to lose her.

catalog.title: Heartless Hunter
catalog.author: Kristen Ciccarelli
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Rune and Gideon, each secretly investigating the other, so the dramatic irony runs both directions from chapter one
catalog.hook: A witch posing as a vapid socialite runs rescue missions for condemned witches at night, and starts courting the witch hunter who is closing in on her.
catalog.caution: It's marketed and paced as YA: closed door, teenage leads, and a plot that moves fast partly because it's short; after Empyrean and Crescent City the emotional register may feel a size too small.

catalog.title: Rebel Witch
catalog.author: Kristen Ciccarelli
catalog.setting: a post-revolutionary state where witches are hunted, modeled on the Terror
catalog.povNote: close third alternating between Rune and Gideon, each one certain the other is the mistake they cannot stop making
catalog.hook: The conclusion of the Crimson Moth duology, in which the vigilante witch and the witch hunter captain who loves her strike a bargain neither can survive keeping.
catalog.caution: Start at Heartless Hunter (2024) or nothing lands, and the duology is shelved YA, so the spice ceiling is roughly where The Bone Witch sat.

catalog.title: Kushiel's Dart
catalog.author: Jacqueline Carey
catalog.setting: Terre d'Ange, an alternate Renaissance France where love as thou wilt is law
catalog.povNote: first person retrospective; Phedre is telling you this years later, which means she survives, and the tension comes from what it cost
contentWarnings: sexual content involving a young adult
catalog.hook: A courtesan trained as a spy, marked by a god to find pleasure in pain, uncovers the conspiracy that will sell her country to invaders, and is betrayed by the person she trusted most.
comps: House of Earth and Blood (scope and political machinery)
The Bone Witch trilogy (the retrospective voice)
catalog.caution: It is a thousand pages, twenty-five years old, and the first hundred are training and naming conventions before the plot engages, plus the on-page sexual content involving a teenage Phedre is a hard line for a lot of modern readers.

catalog.title: The Once and Future Witches
catalog.author: Alix E. Harrow
catalog.povNote: rotating third person across the three Eastwood sisters, each with a genuinely distinct register
catalog.hook: In an alternate 1893 where witching has been beaten down into nursery rhymes, three estranged sisters reclaim lost magic and fuse it to the women's suffrage movement.
catalog.caution: Winner of the British Fantasy Award and genuinely devastating in the back half, but it is 517 pages, the prose is thick with embedded fairy tales, and the sisters spend the first third apart and prickly.

catalog.title: Divine Rivals
catalog.author: Rebecca Ross
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Iris and Roman, who are also writing each other anonymous letters through an enchanted typewriter without knowing who's on the other end
catalog.hook: Two rival newspaper columnists fall for each other through magically delivered letters while reporting from the front line of a war between gods.
catalog.caution: It's closed-door and the tenderness is the point; after Butcher & Blackbird and Lights Out, the complete absence of heat may register as sweet rather than charged, even though the ending hits like a truck.

catalog.title: The Death of Jane Lawrence
catalog.author: Caitlin Starling
catalog.setting: Great Breltain, a post-war alternate England, and the rotting manor of Lindridge Hall
catalog.povNote: tight third on Jane, deliberately unreliable; the reader is never given ground she does not have
tropes: one rule you must not break
catalog.hook: A woman proposes a purely practical marriage to a reclusive surgeon, breaks his single condition on the wedding night, and finds the house is doing something to him.
catalog.caution: The final third abandons plot logic for hallucinatory occult mathematics, and the 3.23 average is almost entirely readers who felt the book stopped answering them.

catalog.title: The Death Club
catalog.author: Caroline Peckham & Susanne Valenti
catalog.povNote: rotating first-person across Brooklyn, Niall and Mateo, with Brooklyn carrying most of the voice
catalog.hook: A woman trafficked and resold repeatedly ends up bought by an Irish mobster who is also a serial killer, and turns out to be more dangerous than either man holding her.
catalog.caution: It is a menage that ends on a hard cliffhanger, and the psychopathy is played broad enough that some readers find the trio immature rather than genuinely unhinged.

catalog.title: Tourist Season
catalog.author: Brynne Weaver
catalog.setting: Cape Carnage, a tourist-choked coastal town in the present-day US
catalog.povNote: alternating first-person between Harper and Nolan, with her interiority doing most of the comedic and emotional lifting
catalog.hook: A gardener who quietly disposes of the town's worst tourists is hunted by the brother of one of her victims, and the two end up covering for each other when a true-crime investigator closes in.
catalog.caution: It is Weaver again, and she DNF'd Leather & Lark at 25%; the banter-forward voice that worked in Butcher & Blackbird is the same voice here, so if that was the thing that soured, this will sour too.

catalog.title: Iron Widow
catalog.author: Xiran Jay Zhao
catalog.setting: Huaxia, a science-fantasy China where giant mecha are piloted by paired boys and disposable girls
catalog.povNote: first person, present tense, entirely Zetian, and her voice is the point: she is never sympathetic and never apologizes
catalog.hook: A girl enlists as a sacrificial mecha co-pilot to murder the boy who killed her sister, survives the pairing that should have killed her, and starts dismantling the system that built it.
catalog.caution: Marketed YA with fade-to-black intimacy and blunt, functional prose; she rates prose quality highly, and this book's line level is its weakest point.

catalog.title: Sinners Retreat
catalog.author: Lauren Biel
catalog.povNote: dual first-person; both of them are lying to the other about why they came to the island
catalog.hook: Two killers who slept together the night before discover they are both attending an island retreat where murderers hunt assigned targets, and one of them knows how her brother died.
catalog.caution: It is openly chasing Butcher & Blackbird and the humor is cruder; several reviewers call it fart jokes where Weaver had wit, so the comparison she will inevitably make works against it.

catalog.title: Starling House
catalog.author: Alix E. Harrow
catalog.povNote: Opal narrates in first person present, Arthur's sections come in third, plus fake footnotes and archival fragments
tropes: haunted house with a will of its own
catalog.hook: A dirt-poor young woman in a dying Kentucky coal town takes a housekeeping job at the haunted mansion everyone avoids and discovers she is tied to the thing it was built to cage.
catalog.caution: The lowest-rated book on this list, and the split is real: the middle stalls on Opal and Arthur refusing to talk to each other, which is exactly the miscommunication engine she has no patience for.

catalog.title: Jane Doe
catalog.author: Victoria Helen Stone
catalog.povNote: first-person from a self-diagnosed sociopath, which is the entire point; the voice is the engine
catalog.hook: A sociopathic international lawyer takes a temp job at a Minneapolis insurance firm under a fake meek persona to systematically dismantle the man who drove her best friend to suicide.
catalog.caution: Single POV and the romance is a subplot, not the spine; if she wants the relationship to carry the book, this will feel like a thriller that happens to have a man in it.

catalog.title: When She Unravels
catalog.author: Gabrielle Sands
catalog.povNote: dual first-person weighted roughly 70/30 toward Valentina
catalog.hook: A woman on the run from an abusive mafia enforcer takes a job at an Ibiza nightclub owned by the island's crime boss, who has his own reason for keeping her.
catalog.caution: The relationship moves in about a month and the hero turns genuinely cruel after a mid-book reveal without earning his way back; she may read that as a character acting against his own established nature.

catalog.title: My Dreadful Darling
catalog.author: H.D. Carlton
catalog.povNote: alternating first person between Reverie and Kellan/'Dread', with his obsession rendered from the inside rather than reported
catalog.hook: The son of a murdered woman enrolls at the same university as the daughter of the man who killed her, intending to ruin her, while a copycat starts working the same town.
catalog.caution: Book two slipped to late 2026 and this ends mid-story; separately, the consent dynamics go further than Haunting Adeline did, which is the ceiling she has actually rated.

catalog.title: One Dark Window
catalog.author: Rachel Gillig
catalog.povNote: first person Elspeth, but she shares her skull with the Nightmare, a second voice that argues with her; it reads closer to two narrators than one; book two, Two Twisted Crowns, opens into true multi-POV
catalog.hook: A woman hiding an infected magic and the ancient monster living inside her joins a prince's bastard cousin in stealing the magic cards that could break her curse.
catalog.caution: Only one POV in book one, and the romance is deliberately underplayed next to the curse plot; if she's reading for the dual-POV push-pull she got from Violet and Xaden, she'll feel the absence until book two.

catalog.title: The Knight and the Moth
catalog.author: Rachel Gillig
catalog.setting: Aisling Cathedral and the surrounding gothic kingdom of Traum
catalog.povNote: first person from Six throughout; the knight stays fully external, which is either the appeal or the dealbreaker
catalog.hook: A girl raised to drown herself for prophecy leaves the cathedral with the knight who says her visions are a lie, and finds out he is right in the worst possible way.
catalog.caution: Single POV and a cliffhanger, and Publishers Weekly flagged the middle as slack; the atmosphere is doing work that plot momentum usually does for her.

catalog.title: Bury Our Bones in the Midnight Soil
catalog.author: V.E. Schwab
catalog.povNote: three women's lives in three centuries, rotating, and the moment you understand how they touch is the moment the book detonates
catalog.hook: Three women across five hundred years are turned into vampires and have to decide what they will do with an appetite nobody asked them to have.
comps: House of Earth and Blood (for scope)
The Bone Witch trilogy (for the cold, controlled prose)
catalog.caution: Critics who disliked it call it vibes and repetition with no plot; it is a character study, not a momentum engine, and she has said outright she won't wait a book out.

catalog.title: When the Moon Hatched
catalog.author: Sarah A. Parker
catalog.povNote: roughly seventy percent Raeve, with chapters from the king Kaan and interleaved past-life fragments that recontextualise both
catalog.hook: In a world where dragons become moons when they die, a legendary assassin is caught and imprisoned by a king who recognises her from a life she doesn't remember.
catalog.caution: Parker invents her own vocabulary for time, anatomy and geography and drops you in with no glossary; the opening 100 pages are genuinely disorienting, and readers who want momentum from page one are the ones who DNF it.

catalog.title: The Ministry of Time
catalog.author: Kaliane Bradley
catalog.setting: present-day London, inside a secret government department that extracts people from history
catalog.povNote: first person from an unnamed British-Cambodian civil servant, with interleaved Arctic sections from the man she is minding
catalog.hook: A civil servant is assigned to live with a Victorian naval officer pulled out of the moment of his death, and falls for the man she is paid to report on.
comps: The Bone Witch trilogy (the narrator's dry interiority)
catalog.caution: It is a literary novel wearing a spy-thriller coat; the romance is real but structurally secondary, and the 3.55 average is readers who came for a love story and got an essay on empire.

catalog.title: Lovesick
catalog.author: Trisha Wolfe
catalog.setting: Stonehurst University, a dark-academia campus in the present-day US
catalog.povNote: alternating first person between the undercover analyst and the astrophysicist she is building a case against
catalog.hook: An FBI crime analyst embeds as a campus therapist to work the astrophysicist she believes is a serial killer, and finds the investigation running in both directions.
catalog.caution: It is indie and small; under three hundred ratings, so the average is soft and the line-level prose has not been stress-tested the way her other picks have.

catalog.title: Say You're Sorry
catalog.author: Karen Rose
catalog.povNote: third-person rotating between Daisy, Gideon and the killer, so the reader is always ahead of someone
catalog.hook: A woman who fights off an attacker and keeps his locket draws in an FBI agent who recognizes it from the cult he escaped as a child, and the two of them chase a serial killer.
catalog.caution: This is traditional Berkley romantic suspense; 600-plus pages, characters re-litigating the same conversations, and the spice and moral blackness are both several notches below what she reads for.

catalog.title: A Fate Inked in Blood
catalog.author: Danielle L. Jensen
catalog.povNote: Freya carries the bulk of the narration with Bjorn's POV threaded in, so you see him working her while she's working him
catalog.hook: A blacksmith's wife with a drop of a goddess's blood is bound by oath to a warlord who intends to use her prophecy to unite Skaland under his rule.
catalog.caution: For the first third Freya is genuinely being moved around the board by men; husband, jarl, Bjorn, and this reader's stated dealbreaker is a heroine who can't act without a man; Freya earns her agency, but she earns it later than this reader likes to wait.

catalog.title: Ninth House
catalog.author: Leigh Bardugo
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Alex Stern in the present and Darlington in the months before he vanished, plus a shifting timeline
catalog.hook: A Yale freshman with a criminal past and the ability to see ghosts is recruited to police the university's occult secret societies, then investigates a townie's murder nobody else wants solved.
catalog.caution: Alex is guarded to the point of coldness for a long stretch and the first third is dense with society lore, so the emotional attachment she needs arrives later than her patience usually allows; the sexual violence is also far more graphic than anything in her current shelf.

catalog.title: Gideon the Ninth
catalog.author: Tamsyn Muir
catalog.povNote: close third on Gideon only, which is the engine of the book because she understands almost nothing of the necromancy happening around her
catalog.hook: An indentured swordswoman is dragged along as bodyguard to the bone witch who rules her dying House, into a crumbling palace where necromancers and their cavaliers are being murdered one by one.
catalog.caution: The first hundred pages deliberately withhold the rules of the world and the voice is aggressively irreverent, so if she wants emotional grip early this one makes her earn it before the ending lands like a hammer.

catalog.title: The Jasmine Throne
catalog.author: Tasha Suri
catalog.povNote: Priya and Malini carry the book, with rotating chapters from a rebel leader, a noblewoman and a prince that make the politics real rather than decorative
catalog.hook: An exiled princess plotting her brother's overthrow and the temple-born maidservant assigned to her cell each decide the other is the weapon they need.
comps: The Priory of the Orange Tree
catalog.caution: The romance is a long fuse inside a genuinely political novel; nobody gets rescued and both women are terrifying, but the first 150 pages move at empire speed, not Basgiath speed.

catalog.title: Black Sheep
catalog.author: Alexa Harlowe & Brynne Weaver
catalog.povNote: dual first-person; she is hunting a cult leader as a killer, he is hunting the same man for the FBI
catalog.hook: A doctoral student who kills cult members and the professor secretly investigating the same cult for the FBI close in on the same target and on each other.
catalog.caution: The thriller half is thin; the revenge arc has real logic gaps and the romance swallows the investigation, which is the opposite of what made Mindf*ck work for her.

catalog.title: Marrow
catalog.author: Trisha Wolfe & Brynne Weaver
catalog.povNote: first-person alternating between two rival killers who are each hiding what they are from the other
catalog.hook: A forensic anthropologist and a wildlife biologist who have spent three years trying to out-kill each other at a university body farm are forced into an alliance against a shared threat.
catalog.caution: Reviewers repeatedly call it light on plot; it is almost entirely the two of them circling each other, and the MMC is noticeably less developed than the FMC.

catalog.title: The Blood Trials
catalog.author: N.E. Davenport
catalog.povNote: first person present from Ikenna, tight and furious, no hero chapters
tropes: found family in a kill-or-be-killed cohort
catalog.hook: A young woman enters a brutal military trial to find out who assassinated her grandfather, while hiding the outlawed blood magic that would get her executed on sight.
catalog.caution: Single POV and the romance is a genuine subplot rather than the engine; she gets the Basgiath-style trials and the rage, but not the slow-cooked tension between two heads she reread Empyrean twenty times for.

catalog.title: The Bridge Kingdom
catalog.author: Danielle L. Jensen
catalog.povNote: alternating first-person between Lara, the assassin-bride sent to destroy the kingdom, and Aren, the king she married to destroy
catalog.hook: A princess raised from childhood as a weapon marries the king of the kingdom she was trained to bring down, and has to decide which of her loyalties is actually hers.
catalog.caution: The prose is functional rather than beautiful; Jensen writes clean, propulsive plot, not sentences you reread, and after Quicksilver landed at a 3 for her, workmanlike writing may be the exact thing that caps this at four stars.

catalog.title: The Diviners
catalog.author: Libba Bray
catalog.povNote: rotating third person across Evie, Memphis, Theta, Sam, Mabel and Jericho, with occasional omniscient interludes from objects and weather
catalog.hook: In 1926 Manhattan, a flapper who can read a person's secrets by touching their belongings is pulled into hunting an occult serial killer alongside a group of young people hiding supernatural gifts of their own.
catalog.caution: It is the same author she already rated 4, but it is 578 pages with six POV threads that do not converge until late, and the romance is a background flicker at best across the whole quartet.

catalog.title: Nettle & Bone
catalog.author: T. Kingfisher
catalog.povNote: close third on Marra, a thirty-year-old princess nobody ever bothered to watch
catalog.hook: A forgotten youngest princess builds a dog out of bones, sews a cloak of nettles and assembles a party of oddballs in order to murder her sister's abusive royal husband.
catalog.caution: Hugo winner, genuinely funny and dark at once, but Marra is quiet and middle-aged in spirit, the romance is a slow warm afterthought, and the stakes are domestic rather than world-shaking.

catalog.title: Spinning Silver
catalog.author: Naomi Novik
catalog.povNote: six first-person narrators with unmarked chapter switches, led by Miryem, Wanda and Irina
catalog.hook: A Jewish moneylender's daughter who turns silver into gold too well attracts the attention of the winter king, and her fate braids together with a peasant girl's and a tsarina's.
catalog.caution: Three heroines with maximum agency and no rescuing, but the narrators are unlabelled and the romances are cold, restrained and mostly implied, which after Empyrean may read as emotionally withholding.

catalog.title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
catalog.author: Samantha Shannon
catalog.povNote: four principal narrators across two hemispheres; a bodyguard-mage, an Eastern dragonrider, a disgraced alchemist and a courtier; braided toward one convergence
tropes: dragons on both sides of a culture war
queen who must produce an heir
catalog.hook: Across a divided world where the East reveres dragons and the West fears them, four people race to stop an ancient wyrm from waking.
catalog.caution: 848 pages of genuine epic fantasy where the romance is one thread among many; this is the dragon book for the part of her that loves Tairn and Andarna, not the part that rereads for Violet and Xaden.

catalog.title: These Violent Delights
catalog.author: Chloe Gong
catalog.povNote: third person alternating primarily between Juliette and Roma, with short interludes from Marshall, Kathleen and Benedikt
catalog.hook: In 1926 Shanghai, the heir to the Scarlet Gang and the heir to the rival White Flowers, former lovers who betrayed each other, must work together as a madness drives citizens to tear out their own throats.
catalog.caution: Juliette is a ruthless gangster heir with real command and the dual POV is exactly her preference, but the book front-loads a lot of Shanghai political exposition and the central romance stays frozen in mistrust until very late.

catalog.title: And I Darken
catalog.author: Kiersten White
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Lada and her brother Radu, who want incompatible things from the same man
catalog.hook: Vlad the Impaler reimagined as a girl: Lada Dragwlya and her gentle brother are handed to the Ottoman court as hostages, where she refuses to be anything other than a weapon.
catalog.caution: Lada is the least rescued heroine in this entire lane, but the book is historical court politics with almost no magic and a slow-building love triangle, and the romance never resolves the way romance readers expect.

catalog.title: Silver Under Nightfall
catalog.author: Rin Chupeco
catalog.povNote: first person throughout from Remy Pendergast, the half-outcast vampire hunter
catalog.hook: A despised vampire hunter is forced to investigate a plague turning vampires into unkillable monsters alongside a vampire heiress and her ancient fiance, and falls for both of them.
catalog.caution: This is her Bone Witch author writing with far more romance and heat, but the POV is a man and the female lead Xiaodan is the love interest rather than the driver, which inverts exactly what she liked about Tea.

catalog.title: Katabasis
catalog.author: R.F. Kuang
catalog.setting: Cambridge's department of Analytic Magick, and the eight courts of Hell
catalog.povNote: Alice narrates the present descent; Peter's side arrives through interleaved flashbacks, so the reader learns him at the same rate she is forced to
catalog.hook: Two graduate students in magic walk into Hell to retrieve the advisor they helped kill, mostly because they still need his letter of recommendation.
catalog.caution: The romance is a subplot carried almost entirely in subtext and flashback; she wants the build to matter, and here the build is competing with two hundred pages of footnoted logic puzzles.

catalog.title: Nocticadia
catalog.author: Keri Lake
catalog.povNote: dual first-person between Lilia and the professor known as Doctor Death
catalog.hook: A student enrolls at a remote gothic university in Maine to investigate the parasite she believes killed her mother, and ends up circling the pathologist at the center of it.
catalog.caution: It is 680 pages and the leads barely interact for the first 40 percent; exactly the slow build she has said she will not wait through.

catalog.title: Midnight Is the Darkest Hour
catalog.author: Ashley Winstead
catalog.povNote: Ruth's first person across a split timeline, past and present braided
catalog.hook: A preacher's daughter and the town outcast she has loved since childhood have to protect a shared secret when a skull surfaces in the Louisiana swamp.
catalog.caution: The prose is the best on this list but the rating is the lowest for a reason; it is slow, the twist is telegraphed, and the romance is atmospheric rather than propulsive.

catalog.title: Master of Crows
catalog.author: Grace Draven
catalog.povNote: third person split between Martise, the bondwoman sent to spy, and Silhara, the sorcerer who knows exactly what she is and lets her stay
catalog.hook: A bondwoman is promised her freedom if she will spy on a renegade sorcerer, who needs her help to keep a hungry god from taking his body.
catalog.caution: It's a fifteen-plus-year-old self-published title and reads it; the pacing is unhurried, the world is small, and there is none of the cinematic scale she gets from Basgiath or Crescent City.

catalog.title: Still Beating
catalog.author: Jennifer Hartmann
catalog.povNote: dual POV split across a captivity section and a long, messy aftermath section
catalog.hook: Two people who have loathed each other for fifteen years are abducted by a serial killer who forces couples to fall in love, and most of the book is what happens to them after they get out.
catalog.caution: The emotional payoff is real but the premise is a trauma bond plus a betrayed sister, and if she reads the romance as built on captivity rather than on the characters, the whole thing collapses.

catalog.title: An Ember in the Ashes
catalog.author: Sabaa Tahir
catalog.povNote: alternating first person between Laia, a slave spying inside the military academy, and Elias, the academy's best soldier planning to desert; later books widen to four narrators
catalog.hook: A girl sells herself into slavery inside an empire's military academy to save her brother, and crosses paths with the academy's finest soldier on the eve of deadly succession trials.
catalog.caution: YA and largely closed-door, and the romance is a messy near-square rather than a two-person build; she'd be reading it for the deaths that land and the Basgiath-adjacent institution, not for the tension.

catalog.title: Alchemised
catalog.author: SenLinYu
catalog.setting: Paladia, a devastated magical nation under occupation after a lost war
catalog.povNote: Helena's present-day POV braided with nonlinear recovered memories and sections from the High Reeve, so the reader assembles the truth ahead of her
catalog.hook: A captured Resistance healer with a hole in her memory is handed to the enemy's chief necromancer, who wants to know what she buried in her own head.
comps: Onyx Storm (for the devastation, not the tone)
catalog.caution: Over a thousand pages built on a heroine who spends the first act imprisoned and passive; her 'no waiting for the back half' rule is exactly what this book asks her to break.

catalog.title: Bad Men
catalog.author: Julie Mae Cohen
catalog.povNote: alternates between Saffy and Jonathan, with more page time on him than the premise promises
catalog.hook: A socialite who kills abusive men engineers a meeting with the true-crime podcaster she is obsessed with after body parts turn up on his doorstep and make him a suspect.
catalog.caution: Traditionally published and genuinely well-written, but it is low-spice and comic; the stakes never bite the way the Mindf*ck books do, so a death here will not land.

catalog.title: The Irresistible Urge to Fall For Your Enemy
catalog.author: Brigitte Knightley
catalog.setting: a secondary world of rival magical orders; assassins on one side, healers on the other
catalog.povNote: close third alternating between Aurienne the healer and Osric the assassin, with both voices distinct enough to be told apart blind
catalog.hook: A dying assassin bribes the healer who despises him into curing him, and the two spend a book dissecting each other; clinically and otherwise, while a pox spreads.
comps: The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System (for the tone of the sniping)
catalog.caution: The payoff is one scene near the very end; if her 'the build matters more than the payoff' has a floor, this book sits right on it, and readers who wanted heat left the 3.79 average.

catalog.title: Mexican Gothic
catalog.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
catalog.povNote: close third limited entirely to Noemi, so the house's secrets unspool only as fast as she pries them loose
catalog.hook: A glamorous 1950s Mexico City socialite travels to a decaying mansion in the mountains to rescue her cousin from a family of English mine owners, and finds the house itself is feeding on them.
catalog.caution: Award-decorated and atmospheric, but the first half is deliberately claustrophobic and nothing supernatural is confirmed for a long time, and there is essentially no romance to carry her through that stretch.

catalog.title: The Cruel Prince
catalog.author: Holly Black
catalog.povNote: first person from Jude, whose scheming is the plot rather than a reaction to it
catalog.hook: A human girl raised in the High Court of Faerie by the man who murdered her parents claws her way toward power by outmaneuvering the cruel prince who torments her.
catalog.caution: Zero spice and the romance is mostly antagonism until the final act, so this rides entirely on whether Jude's ruthlessness carries her; if she needs an emotional anchor in the male lead early, Cardan is deliberately unlovable for most of book one.

catalog.title: Radiance
catalog.author: Grace Draven
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Ildiko and Brishen, who each privately find the other hideous and say so
catalog.hook: A human noblewoman and a Kai prince are married off to seal a treaty neither wanted, and build a real partnership out of dry humour and mutual respect before either finds the other attractive.
catalog.caution: Book one is deliberately low-stakes and domestic; the series' devastating turns arrive in Eidolon, and she has said she will not wait through a slow build for a back-half payoff, let alone a next-book one.

catalog.title: The Maddest Obsession
catalog.author: Danielle Lori
catalog.povNote: genuinely balanced dual POV between Gianna and Christian, unlike book one's lopsided split
catalog.hook: A chaotic, sharp-tongued mafia daughter and the undercover agent who has been quietly obsessed with her for years finally stop dodging each other.
catalog.caution: It is book two of a connected series and the darkness is atmospheric rather than violent, after Mindf*ck and Haunting Adeline this may read as too tame to count as dark.

prerequisite.needsTitle: The Sweetest Oblivion (reads standalone, but book 1 gives context)

catalog.title: Rose in Chains
catalog.author: Julie Soto
catalog.povNote: third person Briony, cutting between present-day captivity and flashbacks to the magic academy where she and her captor were classmates
catalog.hook: After her kingdom falls, a princess stripped of her magic is auctioned to a member of the conquering faction who turns out to have known her before the war.
catalog.caution: Another captivity premise where the heroine's power is scheming rather than acting; she plots beautifully but she is in chains, and this reader has already said she loses patience with a woman who needs someone else to open the door.

catalog.title: A Winter's Promise
catalog.author: Christelle Dabos
catalog.setting: the Ark of the Pole, a frozen sky-island court, after the world shattered into floating fragments
catalog.povNote: third limited on Ophelia with brief excursions; Thorn is kept opaque for most of the quartet by design, and the reveal of his interiority is the series' long payoff
catalog.hook: Translated from the French by Hildegarde Serle: a clumsy museum curator who can read objects' histories is shipped across the world into an arranged marriage she was chosen for by someone with a plan.
catalog.caution: It is a genuinely slow, cold, four-book arc with zero spice and a heroine whose agency is subtle rather than kinetic; everything she says she needs early, this book withholds on purpose.

catalog.title: When Heroes Fall
catalog.author: Giana Darling
catalog.povNote: dual first-person between the defense lawyer and the capo she is defending
catalog.hook: A cold, ferociously competent defense attorney takes on a mafia capo accused of murder and is required to live in his house while he is under arrest.
catalog.caution: The prose swings purple and the first half is slow; the exact combination that made her DNF Leather & Lark at 25 percent.

catalog.title: The Hurricane Wars
catalog.author: Thea Guanzon
catalog.povNote: third person alternating between Talasyn, the light-magic soldier, and Alaric, the heir to the empire that burned her home
catalog.hook: A soldier who can wield light magic and the crown prince of the shadow empire hunting her are forced into a marriage alliance when their opposing powers turn out to fuse.
catalog.caution: The first third is almost pure worldbuilding and the burn is genuinely slow; this is the single book on the list most likely to trip her stated rule about not waiting for a back-half payoff.

catalog.title: Born, Darkly
catalog.author: Trisha Wolfe
catalog.povNote: alternating first-person between the psychologist and the death-row killer she is evaluating
catalog.hook: A criminal psychologist treating a death-row serial killer who only kills predators finds his games reshaping her faster than her analysis reshapes him.
catalog.caution: It opens slow, the thriller keeps elbowing the romance aside, and it ends on a cliffhanger into book two; three separate ways for her to lose patience early.

catalog.title: There Are No Saints
catalog.author: Sophie Lark
catalog.povNote: dual first-person; his chapters are the stalking, hers are the not-knowing
catalog.hook: A celebrated San Francisco artist who kills for pleasure fixes on a struggling painter after a rival serial killer attacks her, and installs himself as her mentor.
catalog.caution: This is the prose problem title on the list; reviewers consistently call the writing choppy and the leads one-dimensional, which is her single biggest complaint about a book.

catalog.title: We Who Will Die
catalog.author: Stacia Stark
catalog.povNote: first person Arvelle only, though the audiobook uses duet narration that can make it feel broader than it is
catalog.hook: Bound by a blood vow to assassinate the emperor, a young woman fights her way through a magical gladiator tournament in a Rome ruled by vampires to reach his personal guard.
comps: The Serpent and the Wings of Night
catalog.caution: Single POV, and reviewers consistently say the back half rushes; big events land and the book immediately moves on, which blunts exactly the deaths and betrayals she reads for.

catalog.title: Shield of Sparrows
catalog.author: Devney Perry
catalog.setting: the kingdoms of Quentis and Turah, separated by monster-infested wilds
catalog.povNote: Odessa carries essentially the whole book; the male lead gets one late chapter, so calling it dual POV is marketing
catalog.hook: A disregarded princess is married off to a hostile kingdom as a political shield and falls for her betrothed's guardian on the road there.
catalog.caution: Multiple reviewers say nothing happens until the last 30 percent and the heroine is reactive for most of it; this is the exact shape of the slow build she has said she will not sit through.
